# Signet 01

A sterling silver signet ring with a signing chip in its face. Designed by Jim Hannon-Tan in Adelaide.

Jim Hannon-Tan is a designer who has worked with Alessi, Tom Dixon, LVMH and Flos.

## What it does

Touch the ring to an NFC-equipped phone to sign words, an image or a document. The person you send it to receives the content and a record they can verify.

1. Choose: select the content and any dedication.
2. Review: see exactly what you are signing and sharing.
3. Sign: touch the ring to your phone to create the signature.
4. Send: share the signed record through a link.

A signed piece can also be minted as an on-chain collectible.

## The object

Cast in sterling silver. The square spiral on the face is the antenna, twelve turns in the metal. There is no battery; the phone powers the chip when you touch them together.

## Technology

- Chip: ARX HaLo secure element. It creates the cryptographic signature.
- Key: secp256k1, generated inside the chip. Cannot be exported or copied.
- Connection: NFC, touched to a phone.
- Phones: supported models will be confirmed before delivery.
- Account: optional. A LUKSO Universal Profile can link the ring to an account, with permissions you set.
- Networks: signatures can be checked on LUKSO, Ethereum and Base, and by web services that support them.
- Verification: checks the signing key, and whether the content matches the signed record.
- Limits: a signature shows that this ring signed this content. On its own it does not establish original authorship or verified legal identity.
- Status: signing on the chip is demonstrated. The Signet application is in development.

Other software could use the same chip for logging in to accounts, approving wallet transactions, showing membership, or approving an action that a person or an AI agent has prepared. None of these work with Signet 01 yet.

## Edition 01

Twenty rings, numbered 01 to 20. USD 4,800. Delivery from Q1 2027.
